_about: Every visible string of the Prepare element pages (spec 5.2): the inventory template, the migration approach (off the Atlas since 5 October 2026, kept for its return at /elsewhere/approach, linked from no Atlas page), the supplier letter and the guides, under copy; and the supplier letter’s questions under questions, keyed by the id of the Readiness Check action each is drawn from, each with the source’s own words read on 1 October 2026; and under notes, the passage the letter’s statement of intent line rests on. A source’s own words are kept for review only: the pages show them inside SourceWords, which a production build leaves out. A question’s cite is the short locator in its bracketed source tag. A {milestone:id} placeholder is filled from that milestone’s year in readiness.json, so a date is kept once.

suppliers.question: What to ask your suppliers
suppliers.lede: What {guides} published guides ask an organisation to raise with its suppliers, as questions you can send, each with its source in brackets.
suppliers.description: Questions to send to suppliers about post-quantum cryptography, drawn from published migration guidance, each with its source in brackets. Printable, with nothing sent or stored.
suppliers.why: For many organisations, much of the cryptography they rely on is in what they buy: embedded in products and equipment, delivered in software and firmware updates, or run by cloud and managed service providers. An organisation’s own move to post-quantum cryptography therefore depends on what its suppliers do, and when: the EU roadmap asks every organisation to start talking to its suppliers for that reason, and the NCSC expects an organisation’s plan to move as its suppliers’ plans change. The inventory needs their answers too: discovery tools may not find cryptography embedded inside a product, so the CISA, NSA and NIST factsheet advises asking vendors to list it. Procurement and contracts are where an organisation can ask: the Canadian roadmap advises putting post-quantum requirements into new procurements, and the factsheet advises planning changes to existing and future contracts, so that new products arrive with post-quantum cryptography built in.
suppliers.chooserLegend: Choose the guides whose questions go in the letter
suppliers.chooserHint: {guides} are chosen to start with, as in the Readiness Check.
suppliers.paragraphLabel: Covering paragraph, which you can edit
suppliers.paragraph: We are preparing to move our systems to post-quantum cryptography, which protects information against a future quantum computer able to break today’s public-key encryption. Much of that move depends on the products and services you supply to us, so we would be grateful for your answers to the questions below.
suppliers.paragraphNote: Edit it here. It stays in this page: it is not saved, not sent and not put in any link.
suppliers.intentText: The NCSC suggests you could also share a statement of intent: how you see the quantum threat, how you plan to respond, your ambition and timelines, and the end state you want. It says this helps suppliers understand the demand and bring post-quantum products to market.
suppliers.empty: Choose at least one guide to see its questions.

suppliers.copyFailed: The letter could not be copied here. Download it as a text file instead.

suppliers.method1: Each question is the Atlas’s plain wording of something a guide asks an organisation to raise with its suppliers; the brackets name the guide and the place in it. The paragraph on why to ask rests only on what the guides say about suppliers, products and contracts.
suppliers.method2: The questions are a starting point to edit, drop or add to before you send anything. The letter carries no sender, address or sign-off: those are yours to add outside this page. Your choice of guides is kept in the page’s address, so a copied link opens the same letter; the covering paragraph stays in the page.
